key_concepts: The Earth has three layers: crust, mantle, and core.
The crust and upper mantle form the lithosphere.
The liquid part of the mantle and outer core form the asthenosphere.
The Earth's crust is broken into tectonic plates that move 5 to 10 centimeters per year.
Tectonic plates interact at convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries.
Heat and pressure in the asthenosphere cause convection currents in molten rocks.
Movement of molten rocks breaks rocks along faults or cracks and produces seismic waves.
An earthquake is the shaking of the Earth's crust caused by sudden movement of plates rele
The focus is the underground point where an earthquake originates.
The epicenter is the point on the surface directly above the focus where shaking is strong
Tectonic earthquakes result from sudden rock movement or colliding plates.
Volcanic earthquakes result from magma movement within volcanoes.
